item.title: The Weekly Juventus Digest: Six points off fourth, and a fortnight to fix it
item.description: Juventus drew 2-2 at Fiorentina to sit seventh, six points off fourth, as Spalletti faces growing scrutiny heading into the international break and a home game with Venezia.

item.title: The Weekly Inter Digest: Inter give Como the ball and take the points
item.description: Inter beat Como 2-0 with only 43 percent of the ball to go into the international break a point behind Lazio, with Sarri's injury-hit Atalanta up next.

item.title: The Weekly Como Digest: Back to earth at San Siro: what Inter exposed, and what the break must fix
item.description: Four days after a record 9-1 at Lens, Como lost 2-0 at Inter, ending a six-game winning run and dropping to fifth before the November break.

item.title: The Weekly AC Milan Digest: Amorim's split season: a Serie A contender, a Europa League emergency
item.description: Milan sit fourth on 24 points after winning at Genoa, but a 2-0 home loss to Ferencvaros leaves them 28th in the Europa League and Amorim admitting the squad is not ready.

item.title: The Weekly PSG Digest: Eleven straight wins, and PSG did it without their stars
item.description: PSG reach the international break on an 11-match winning run built without Kvaratskhelia, Dembélé and Marquinhos, and will not buy a winter replacement for the Georgian.

item.title: The Weekly Borussia Dortmund Digest: Two tight wins, 21 points and the closest title race in years
item.description: Dortmund beat Real Betis and Elversberg 2-1 to stay level with Bayern on 21 points, but fatigue and injuries to Guirassy and Chukwuemeka cloud the international break.

item.title: The Weekly Bayern Munich Digest: Kane signs on to 2029 as Bayern lead the table into a bruising break
item.description: Harry Kane extends to 2029 at a reported club-record salary while Bayern lead the Bundesliga on goal difference without Kompany, Neuer, Musiala and Saibari.

item.title: The Weekly Arsenal Digest: Five Clear, Seven Clean Sheets, One Winger Missing
item.description: Arsenal reach the last international break of the year top of the Premier League on 27 points, five clear, with the meanest defence in the division and Bukayo Saka still weeks away.

item.title: The Weekly Real Madrid Digest: Eight in a row, and Mourinho's Madrid have found a shape
item.description: Real Madrid head into the November break on an eight-game winning run, three points behind Barcelona, with Diomande's rise and Vinicius's slump the key questions.

item.title: The Weekly Barcelona Digest: Fermín's double at the Metropolitano sends Barça into the break three points clear
item.description: Fermín scored twice in his 100th La Liga game as Barcelona came from behind to win 2-1 at Atlético and go into the break three points clear.

item.title: The Weekly Atletico Madrid Digest: Two Nights at the Metropolitano, One Hard Lesson
item.description: Back-to-back home defeats to Bayern and Barcelona ended a seven-game league winning run and exposed the gap Simeone admits still exists.

item.title: The Weekly Manchester United Digest: Carrick's reprieve runs into the international break
item.description: United go into the international break 18th after a 4-4 draw with Villa, and the board will reassess Michael Carrick's position before the trip to Liverpool.

item.title: The Weekly Manchester City Digest: Seven up, three down: what has gone wrong for Maresca's City
item.description: Seven straight wins have turned into three defeats as Forest beat City 3-1, exposing structural flaws and new defensive injuries before a brutal run of fixtures.

item.title: The Weekly Liverpool Digest: Liverpool find an answer at Selhurst, but the set-piece leak still stings
item.description: After losing to Arsenal and Fenerbahce, Liverpool won 3-1 at Crystal Palace to sit fourth, nine points behind Arsenal, with set-piece defending still their biggest worry.

item.title: The Weekly Chelsea Digest: No striker, no spark: Chelsea stall at the Stadium of Light
item.description: Sunderland's 1-0 win sent Chelsea into the international break fifth and 11 points behind Arsenal, with the absence of João Pedro badly felt.

item.title: The Weekly Soccer Digest: Three clubs, three points, and Atletico host Barcelona on Sunday
item.description: La Liga's top three are separated by three points, and Atletico Madrid can go top on Sunday by beating a Barcelona side travelling without the injured Rodri.

item.title: The Weekly Juventus Digest: Ten days on a knife edge: Spalletti's Juventus fight for air
item.description: After a retreat and a rare speech from the chief executive, Juventus beat Napoli and AZ Alkmaar in five days, but a thin squad and a wary club keep Spalletti on edge.

item.title: The Weekly Inter Digest: Stung by the derby, revived in Rotterdam: Inter face Como's test
item.description: After a first league defeat in the derby, Inter rebuilt with a 3-0 win in Rotterdam and now host high-flying Como in a Serie A top-four clash on Sunday.

item.title: The Weekly Como Digest: Nine at Bollaert: Como rewrite the Champions League record book
item.description: Como's 9-1 win at Lens equalled the Champions League record winning margin and set an Italian scoring mark, with a trip to Inter at San Siro up next.

item.title: The Weekly AC Milan Digest: After the derby, the night that decides Milan's European autumn
item.description: Milan beat Inter 3-1 to climb to fifth in Serie A, but sit 24th in the Europa League and must beat unbeaten Ferencváros tonight at San Siro.

item.title: The Weekly PSG Digest: Six goals, ten wins, no Dembélé: PSG's understudies run riot in Villarreal
item.description: Without Dembélé, Kvaratskhelia and Marquinhos, PSG crushed Villarreal 6-0 for a record 20 goals in four Champions League games and a tenth straight win.

item.title: The Weekly Borussia Dortmund Digest: The back four that held Munich now meets Betis and their perfect record
item.description: Dortmund drew 2-2 at Bayern after Niko Kovac switched to a back four, and now host unbeaten Real Betis in the Champions League tonight.

item.title: The Weekly Bayern Munich Digest: In Kompany's absence, Bayern find another gear
item.description: Interim coach Aaron Danks has kept an injury-hit Bayern unbeaten in four games without Vincent Kompany, capped by a 2-0 win at Atlético Madrid.

item.title: The Weekly Real Madrid Digest: Mourinho's Madrid take a six-game charge to Athens
item.description: Real Madrid travel to AEK Athens on a six-game winning run, with Mourinho rotating, Güler and Tchouaméni rested and Vinícius back for Europe.

item.title: The Weekly Barcelona Digest: Villa at the Camp Nou: a patched-up Barça defence meets Europe's form side
item.description: Barça host Aston Villa, perfect in Europe, tonight with four defenders injured, then travel to Atlético for first against second in LaLiga on Sunday.

item.title: The Weekly Atletico Madrid Digest: Bayern come to the Metropolitano with Atlético's midfield stretched thin
item.description: Atlético host Bayern Munich without Romero, Hjulmand and Cardoso, five days before Barcelona visit with first place in La Liga on the line.

item.title: The Weekly Arsenal Digest: Fourteen Years, One Goal, And A Defensive Masterclass At Anfield
item.description: Arsenal won 1-0 at Anfield for the first time in 14 years, go three points clear at the top, and get William Saliba back for Prague.

item.title: The Weekly Manchester United Digest: Carrick's Roma reckoning: one night to change the story
item.description: Michael Carrick faces Roma at Old Trafford with United 17th, winless in nine and his position set to be assessed at the international break.

item.title: The Weekly Manchester City Digest: Maresca's first real test: two defeats, a lost lead and a trip to Leipzig
item.description: After losses at Villa and at home to Brighton, City have dropped to second behind Arsenal, and Enzo Maresca must fix a leaky defence before facing RB Leipzig.

item.title: The Weekly Liverpool Digest: No shot on target, no answer: Arsenal expose Liverpool's Anfield problem
item.description: Arsenal won 1-0 at Anfield after an Alisson error, Liverpool failed to register a shot on target, and a home attack with four league goals in five games now heads to Istanbul.

item.title: The Weekly Chelsea Digest: Lavia, Rogers and a rare clean sheet: how Alonso steadied a lurching week
item.description: Chelsea beat ten-man Manchester United 2-0 after a week of a Spurs defeat and a Carabao Cup shootout exit, with Lavia and Rogers leading the way before a trip to Sunderland.

item.title: The Weekly Soccer Digest: Der Klassiker arrives level, and without the man who built Bayern's season
item.description: Bayern and Dortmund meet level on points and both unbeaten in a Klassiker Vincent Kompany will watch from home, with Aaron Danks in the dugout.

item.title: The Weekly Soccer Digest: Kane's Crown, and the Klassiker That Follows
item.description: Harry Kane collected the Ballon d'Or in London on Monday and now walks into a first-against-second Klassiker at the Allianz Arena with Bayern's head coach in hospital.

item.title: The Weekly Arsenal Digest: Anfield, Without Him
item.description: Arsenal go to Anfield on Sunday level on points with Manchester City but without Bukayo Saka, who faces weeks out with a quad injury.

item.title: The Weekly Soccer Digest: Mourinho Walks Back Into the Camp Nou
item.description: Jose Mourinho takes Real Madrid back to the Camp Nou on Sunday six points adrift of an unbeaten Barcelona and without Vinicius Junior.

item.title: The Weekly Arsenal Digest: Back to Munich, Carrying a Different Kind of Problem
item.description: Arsenal go to the Allianz Arena as English champions with a perfect Champions League record and a scoring problem nobody has solved yet.

item.title: The Weekly Soccer Digest: The champions of Europe walk into the one place nobody is losing
item.description: Paris Saint-Germain, winners of the last two Champions Leagues, visit an unbeaten Manchester City on a matchday that has already produced 32 goals in nine games.

item.title: The Weekly Arsenal Digest: A new contract, two wins in four days, and the answer last month's defeat demanded
item.description: Arsenal followed Mikel Arteta's new contract to 2030 with a comeback win over Leeds and a 3-0 Champions League rout of Lille, in a week that ended with the death of Ken Friar.

item.title: The Weekly Soccer Digest: The clock started at 7pm on Thursday
item.description: Manchester City lodged their appeal against the guilty verdict at 7pm on 1 October, starting a twelve-week clock that will decide when, and how hard, any punishment lands.

item.title: The Weekly Arsenal Digest: Twenty-one days to fix the thing nobody has fixed
item.description: Arsenal return from a three week international break second in the table with eight goals in five games and the sharpest question of their season still unanswered.
